newsitem.title: FRANCE: AXA says offer for UAP looks successful.
newsitem.headline: AXA says offer for UAP looks successful.

text.p: Insurer Axa said on Wednesday that its exchange offer for UAP shares that closes today appeared to have been very successful.
"The results will be published on January 13, 1997, but it is widely acknowledged to have been very successful," Axa said in a statement.
Axa and UAP said the name of the new holding company stemming from the merger between the two insurers would be Axa-UAP but the group will use the name Axa as its brand name.

"Given the increasingly global nature of business and markets, it is essential that the new group ultimately use a single brand name around the world. This single brand name will be Axa and the gradual transition toward its adoption will vary as a function of local market conditions," it said.
Axa and Union des Assurances de Paris said in November they would merge in a deal initially valued at 40 billion francs ($7.6 billion).
The agreement creates the world's second largest insurer, with annual premium income of more than 300 billion francs.

As previously announced, the new holding firm will have a supervisory board and an executive board. The supervisory board will appoint the executive board and oversee group management. The executive board assisted by an executive committee will be responsible for managing the group.

It will be proposed that UAP chairman Jacques Friednmann be appointed chairman of the supervisory board and Jean-Pierre Ruault, the group's corporate secretary, act as its secretary. ($ = 5.234 French Francs)
